modules.title: How backends work
modules.outcome: Trace a request from a customer action to a saved result.

modules.title: Data foundations
modules.outcome: Explain relationships and protect stored data from invalid changes.

modules.title: Identity and security
modules.outcome: Protect identities, ownership, secrets and sensitive data.

modules.title: Catalog and cart
modules.outcome: Model sellable items, quantities, carts and trustworthy totals.

modules.title: Checkout and payments
modules.outcome: Handle verified payments, duplicates and uncertain outcomes.

modules.title: Orders and fulfillment
modules.outcome: Keep orders, stock, shipments and refunds consistent.

modules.title: Async work and integrations
modules.outcome: Finish background work reliably when other systems fail.

modules.title: Speed and scale
modules.outcome: Measure bottlenecks and improve speed without losing correctness.

modules.title: Testing and debugging
modules.outcome: Prove behavior and investigate failures with useful evidence.

modules.title: Delivery and operations
modules.outcome: Release changes, recover data and operate the store.

modules.title: Working precisely with AI
modules.outcome: Specify, inspect, verify and improve AI-assisted changes.

modules.title: Assemble the complete backend
modules.outcome: Connect the parts and demonstrate an end-to-end working store.

modules.title: Local development and project setup
modules.outcome: Start Fieldstore deliberately and locate failures using the actual project and runtime.

modules.title: Environment variables and secrets
modules.outcome: Classify configuration, load it predictably, and prevent cross-environment secret exposure.

modules.title: Connect a Next.js backend
modules.outcome: Trace UI actions through trusted server operations and explicit HTTP contracts.

modules.title: Supabase database and access
modules.outcome: Choose a connection path and prove database grants, constraints, and ownership policies.

modules.title: Supabase authentication lifecycle
modules.outcome: Verify sessions and safely manage sign-in, callbacks, roles, and account lifecycle.

modules.title: Supabase storage and server tools
modules.outcome: Protect files and use realtime and functions only where their boundaries are understood.

modules.title: Vercel deployment lifecycle
modules.outcome: Diagnose builds, environment scope, server execution and release behavior without deploying.

modules.title: Render services and workers
modules.outcome: Choose a service type and diagnose startup, health, storage and worker failures.

modules.title: Connect the architecture
modules.outcome: Place responsibilities, credentials and data connections in a stack justified by the store.

modules.title: Book a shipment safely
modules.outcome: Prepare, quote and book a synthetic Shiprocket shipment with reliable identifiers and recovery.

modules.title: Tracking, returns and COD
modules.outcome: Handle delivery exceptions, returns, money and stock without confusing their separate states.

modules.title: Connect a payment provider
modules.outcome: Connect trusted checkout totals to verified payment, refund and settlement evidence.

modules.title: Email, SMS and notifications
modules.outcome: Send useful customer messages once per intent and distinguish acceptance from delivery.

modules.title: Networking and security in practice
modules.outcome: Diagnose browser and service boundaries without weakening access or exposing secrets.

modules.title: Operate and recover the store
modules.outcome: Investigate incidents, recover work and prove that business records agree.

modules.title: The connected Fieldstore capstone
modules.outcome: Trace one purchase from signup to refund with permissions, failures and verification.

glossary.meaning: A defined way for software to request data or actions from other software.
The agreed request shape, response shape, errors and behavior of an interface.
A database rule that rejects invalid stored data.
Several operations happening during overlapping time periods.
A group of database changes committed or rolled back together.
Verifying which identity is making a request.
Deciding whether that identity may perform this action on this resource.
A way to associate several requests with an authenticated user.
A rule that must remain true across allowed operations.
Repeating the same logical operation has no additional intended effect.
An external system sends an HTTP notification to your application.
Comparing independent records to find and resolve differences.
A queue holds pending work; a worker executes it separately from the customer request.
Wait longer between retries and vary that delay to spread retry traffic.
A record of work to publish, saved in the same transaction as the business change.
A place for repeatedly failing jobs that require investigation or controlled replay.
A temporary copy of data used to reduce repeated work.
A database structure that accelerates selected queries at storage and write cost.
A versioned change to database structure or stored data.
Using logs, metrics and traces to understand a running system.
Automated checks and a controlled process for preparing and releasing changes.
Targets for acceptable data loss and time to restore service.
Returning application behavior to an earlier known state, where compatible.
The authoritative record for a fact; copies and caches may lag behind.

sources.title: MDN: HTTP overview
sources.note: Network prework and Part 1: requests, responses and the client/server model.

sources.title: MDN: HTTP methods and status codes
sources.note: Part 1: method semantics. Also see the linked MDN HTTP status-code reference.

sources.title: OWASP: Authorization
sources.note: Part 3: deny by default, object ownership and server-side permission checks.

sources.title: OWASP: Session management
sources.note: Security prework and Part 3: sessions, cookie controls and session lifecycle.

sources.title: OWASP: Authentication and recovery
sources.note: Security prework: credential handling and safe authentication behavior.

sources.title: OWASP: REST security and file uploads
sources.note: Security prework and Parts 3 and 8: validation, limits and safe API behavior. File upload companion: cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/File_Upload_Cheat_Sheet.html

sources.title: PostgreSQL: Transactions
sources.note: Part 2: all-or-nothing groups of database changes. Examples are conceptual; use your database documentation.

sources.title: PostgreSQL: Constraints
sources.note: Part 2: primary keys, foreign keys, uniqueness and validation at the data boundary.

sources.title: PostgreSQL: Indexes and isolation
sources.note: Parts 2 and 8: query acceleration and tradeoffs. Isolation companion: postgresql.org/docs/current/transaction-iso.html

sources.title: Shopify: Product variants
sources.note: Parts 4 and 6: options, sellable variants and inventory. Used as a domain reference, not a required platform.

sources.title: Shopify: Inventory states
sources.note: Parts 4 and 6: distinguish physical stock, commitments and availability. Exact terms vary by platform.

sources.title: Stripe: Webhooks
sources.note: Part 5: signatures, retries, duplicate notifications and ordering. Confirm the chosen provider's actual contract.

sources.title: Stripe: Idempotent requests
sources.note: Part 5: stable request keys and safe retry behavior. Retention windows and API semantics are provider-specific.

sources.title: AWS: Transactional outbox
sources.note: Part 7: persist a business change and pending publication together; make consumers safe for duplicates.

sources.title: AWS: Timeouts, retries and backoff
sources.note: Part 7: bounded retries, jitter and uncertain outcomes after timeouts.

sources.title: OpenTelemetry: Observability concepts
sources.note: Part 9: logs, metrics and traces, with identifiers that connect related work.

sources.title: Playwright: Testing best practices
sources.note: Part 9: verify behavior through independent tests. This is an example testing tool, not a stack requirement.

sources.title: Git: Recording changes
sources.note: Part 10: inspect and record small changes in version control.

sources.title: PostgreSQL: Backup and restore
sources.note: Part 10: backup methods and recovery. Use your host and database procedures, and test restoration.

sources.title: OWASP: Secrets management
sources.note: Parts 3 and 10: limited access, rotation and avoiding credential leaks.

sources.title: MDN: HTTP caching
sources.note: Cache freshness, validation, private responses, and the limits of cached results.

capstoneModel.quoteAssumptions: One shirt, zero shipping, tax included for this synthetic exercise only.
rules: A cart addition does not reserve stock in this model.
Payment capture confirms allocation; physical shipment consumes it once.
Provider booking is not physical shipment.
Returned goods enter quarantine before sellable inspection.
Refund and settlement states remain separate from order and stock.
All IDs and provider responses are synthetic; no live service is contacted.

advancedTracks.title: Subscriptions and recurring billing
advancedTracks.summary: Extension beyond the single-store foundation: renewals, payment mandates, plan changes, proration, cancellation and failed recurring collection.
advancedTracks.prerequisites: Verified one-time payments, idempotent events, refund ledgers and explicit entitlement rules.

advancedTracks.title: Marketplaces, seller onboarding, commissions and payouts
advancedTracks.summary: Extension beyond the single-store foundation: separate seller identities, seller approval, split funds, platform fees, payout eligibility and reconciliation.
advancedTracks.prerequisites: Ownership policies, financial ledgers, onboarding requirements and provider-supported marketplace capabilities.

advancedTracks.title: Multiple warehouses and split fulfillment
advancedTracks.summary: Extension beyond the single-store foundation: location-level availability, allocation policy, partial shipments, transfers and per-package return tracking.
advancedTracks.prerequisites: Atomic reservation model, inventory movements and stable order-line/fulfillment identities.

advancedTracks.title: International currencies, tax, customs and duties
advancedTracks.summary: Extension beyond the single-store foundation: currency precision, exchange-rate ownership, localized tax rules, import documents and duty responsibilities.
advancedTracks.prerequisites: Trusted quotes, monetary ledgers and business-approved specialist guidance for each market.

advancedTracks.title: Disputes and chargebacks
advancedTracks.summary: Extension beyond the single-store foundation: dispute evidence, response deadlines, reversals, representment and customer-service coordination.
advancedTracks.prerequisites: Payment/refund history, auditable order and delivery evidence, access control and provider dispute documentation.

advancedTracks.title: ERP, accounting and warehouse integrations
advancedTracks.summary: Extension beyond the single-store foundation: system-of-record decisions, external identifiers, synchronization, reconciliation and conflicting updates.
advancedTracks.prerequisites: Outbox/retry patterns, versioned contracts, inventory/finance ledgers and operational replay controls.

advancedTracks.title: Advanced search, event streaming and distributed systems
advancedTracks.summary: Extension beyond the single-store foundation: indexed projections, event retention, replay, partition ordering, service ownership and measurable consistency tradeoffs.
advancedTracks.prerequisites: Query measurement, cache invalidation, idempotent consumers and a demonstrated need for added infrastructure.
